title: 听董大弹胡笳声兼寄语房给事
title_en: Hearing Dong Da Play the Hujia Tune, Also for Secretary Fang
author: 李颀

text_note.zh: 本库题目是《听董大弹胡笳声兼寄语弄房给事》，多一个“弄”字，通行本（如《唐诗三百首》）题作《听董大弹胡笳声兼寄语房给事》。正文里本库“沈沈”通行本作“沉沉”，“雏鴈”作“雏雁”，都是同一个字的不同写法。这里用通行本。
text_note.en: The corpus title has an extra character, nòng (a tune), before "Secretary Fang"; the commonly taught title (as in Three Hundred Tang Poems) does not. In the text, the corpus writes chén chén and yàn (wild goose) in old forms; the taught text uses the modern characters. We follow the taught text.

readings.zh: “一十有八”就是“十又八”，“有”通“又”，读 yòu。
readings.en: In yī shí yòu bā, "ten and eight", this character stands for "and" and is read yòu.

readings.zh: “角”是古代五音（宫、商、角、徵、羽）之一，读 jué，不读 jiǎo。
readings.en: Here it is one of the five old musical notes (gōng, shāng, jué, zhǐ, yǔ), read jué, not jiǎo.

readings.zh: “摵摵”是落叶的声音，一般读 sè sè，也有书读 shè shè。
readings.en: Sè sè is the sound of falling leaves. It is usually read sè; some books give shè.

readings.zh: “川为净其波”是“河流因此平静了波浪”，“为”读 wèi。
readings.en: In chuān wèi jìng qí bō, "the river calms its waves for it", it is read wèi.
In jiāng wǎng, "about to go", it is read jiāng.
In yìng shǒu, "following the hand", it is read yìng.

readings.zh: “散还合”是“散开了又聚拢”，读 huán。
readings.en: In sàn huán hé, "scatter and gather again", it is read huán.

readings.zh: “长风”是远处吹来的大风，读 cháng。
readings.en: In cháng fēng, "a long wind", it is read cháng.
In the place name Chang'an it is read cháng.
In yè yuán it is read yè.

glosses.zh: 蔡女：蔡琰，字文姬，东汉末年的才女。战乱中她被匈奴人掳走，在北方住了十二年，后来被曹操用重金赎回。
glosses.en: Cai Nü: Cai Yan, also called Cai Wenji, a gifted woman of the late Eastern Han. In a time of war she was carried off by the Xiongnu and lived in the north for twelve years, until Cao Cao paid a large ransom to bring her home.

glosses.zh: 胡笳声：胡笳是北方民族吹的一种乐器，声音很悲凉。这里指传说是蔡文姬作的琴曲《胡笳十八拍》。
glosses.en: hú jiā shēng: the hujia is a reed pipe of the northern peoples, with a very sad sound. Here it means the qin tune "Eighteen Songs of the Hujia", said to have been made by Cai Wenji.

glosses.zh: 一十有八拍：一共十八段。拍：乐曲的一段。
glosses.en: yī shí yòu bā pāi: eighteen sections in all. Pāi here is a section of a tune.

glosses.zh: 边草：边塞上的草。
glosses.en: biān cǎo: grass on the frontier.

glosses.zh: 汉使：汉朝派去接蔡文姬的使者。
glosses.en: hàn shǐ: the Han envoy sent to bring Cai Wenji home.

glosses.zh: 断肠：形容非常伤心。
glosses.en: duàn cháng: "breaking the gut", deeply heartbroken.

glosses.zh: 归客：回家的人，指蔡文姬。
glosses.en: guī kè: the one going home, Cai Wenji.

glosses.zh: 古戍：古老的边防营垒。
glosses.en: gǔ shù: an old frontier fort.

glosses.zh: 烽火：边防报警时点起的火。
glosses.en: fēng huǒ: beacon fires lit to warn of attack at the frontier.

glosses.zh: 大荒：广阔荒凉的原野。
glosses.en: dà huāng: the vast, empty wilderness.

glosses.zh: 沉沉：阴沉昏暗的样子。
glosses.en: chén chén: dark and gloomy.

glosses.zh: 拂：轻轻拨动琴弦。
glosses.en: fú: to brush the strings lightly.

glosses.zh: 商、角、羽：古代五音里的三个音，这里指琴上的弦。
glosses.en: shāng, jué, yǔ: three of the five old musical notes; here, strings of the qin.

glosses.zh: 四郊：四周的野外。
glosses.en: sì jiāo: the countryside all around.

glosses.zh: 惊摵摵：秋叶好像被琴声惊动，沙沙地落下。
glosses.en: jīng sè sè: the autumn leaves seem startled by the music and fall rustling.

glosses.zh: 董夫子：对董大的尊称。董大就是董庭兰，唐代有名的琴师，在兄弟中排行第一，所以叫董大。
glosses.en: Dong Fuzi: a respectful name for Dong Da. Dong Da was Dong Tinglan, a famous Tang qin player. Da means "eldest"; he was the eldest of his brothers.

glosses.zh: 通神明：琴声能感动神灵。
glosses.en: tōng shén míng: his music can reach the spirits.

glosses.zh: 窃听来妖精：深山里的精怪也偷偷跑来听。
glosses.en: qiè tīng lái yāo jīng: even spirits of the deep mountains creep out to listen.

glosses.zh: 言迟更速：弹得慢了，又变快了。
glosses.en: yán chí gèng sù: playing slow, then fast again.

glosses.zh: 皆应手：全都随着手指自然弹出，得心应手。
glosses.en: jiē yìng shǒu: everything flows easily from his fingers.

glosses.zh: 将往复旋：曲调好像要走远了，又转了回来。
glosses.en: jiāng wǎng fù xuán: the tune seems about to go away, then turns back.

glosses.zh: 嘶酸：声音嘶哑、悲酸。
glosses.en: sī suān: hoarse and sad.

glosses.zh: 雏雁失群：小雁和雁群走散了。
glosses.en: chú yàn shī qún: a young goose lost from its flock.

glosses.zh: 断绝胡儿恋母声：蔡文姬回汉朝时，不得不留下在北方生的两个孩子。孩子们舍不得母亲，哭得撕心裂肺。
glosses.en: duàn jué hú ér liàn mǔ shēng: when Cai Wenji returned to Han, she had to leave behind the two children she had in the north. They clung to their mother and cried as if their hearts would break.

glosses.zh: 川为净其波：河流也因此平静下波浪。
glosses.en: chuān wèi jìng qí bō: the river calms its waves to listen.

glosses.zh: 罢其鸣：停止了鸣叫。
glosses.en: bà qí míng: stop their singing.

glosses.zh: 乌孙：汉代西域的一个国家。汉朝曾把公主刘细君嫁到乌孙，她远离家乡，写歌表达思乡之苦。
glosses.en: Wusun: a kingdom in the far west in Han times. The Han court married Princess Liu Xijun to its king; far from home, she wrote a song of homesickness.

glosses.zh: 逻娑：吐蕃的都城，就是今天的拉萨。唐朝文成公主远嫁吐蕃，住在这里。
glosses.en: Luosuo: the capital of Tubo, today's Lhasa. The Tang princess Wencheng married into Tubo and lived there.

glosses.zh: 幽音变调：低沉的声音一下子转了调子。
glosses.en: yōu yīn biàn diào: the low, deep sound suddenly changes key.

glosses.zh: 飘洒：轻快洒脱。
glosses.en: piāo sǎ: light and free.

glosses.zh: 雨堕瓦：雨点落在屋瓦上。
glosses.en: yǔ duò wǎ: rain falling on the roof tiles.

glosses.zh: 迸泉：喷涌出来的泉水。
glosses.en: bèng quán: a spring that bursts out.

glosses.zh: 飒飒：风声、水声。
glosses.en: sà sà: the sound of wind or water.

glosses.zh: 木末：树梢。
glosses.en: mù mò: the treetops.

glosses.zh: 呦呦：鹿的叫声。
glosses.en: yōu yōu: the call of a deer.

glosses.zh: 东掖垣：皇宫东边的门下省，给事中就在这里办公。
glosses.en: dōng yè yuán: the East Wing of the palace, the Chancellery, where the secretaries (jishizhong) worked.

glosses.zh: 凤凰池：皇宫里的中书省，也是朝廷重要的部门。
glosses.en: fèng huáng chí: Phoenix Pool, the Secretariat inside the palace, another key office.

glosses.zh: 青琐门：宫门，门上刻着连环花纹，涂成青色。
glosses.en: qīng suǒ mén: a palace gate carved with linked-ring patterns and painted blue-green.

glosses.zh: 高才：才能很高的人，指房给事，就是房琯。给事是给事中，皇帝身边的一种官。
glosses.en: gāo cái: a person of great talent; here Secretary Fang, Fang Guan. A jishizhong was an official close to the emperor.

glosses.zh: 脱略：不放在心上，看得很轻。
glosses.en: tuō lüè: to care little about.

glosses.zh: 日夕：从早到晚，天天。
glosses.en: rì xī: from morning to night, every day.

glosses.zh: 君：你，指董大。
glosses.en: jūn: you; here Dong Da.

translation.zh: 从前蔡文姬作了胡笳曲，
translation.en: Long ago Cai Wenji made the hujia tune,

translation.zh: 一弹就是十八段。
translation.en: eighteen sections from start to end.

translation.zh: 胡人听了，眼泪落在边塞的草上；
translation.en: The northern people wept onto the frontier grass;

translation.zh: 汉朝使者面对要回家的她，伤心欲绝。
translation.en: the Han envoy, facing her as she left for home, was heartbroken.

translation.zh: 古老的营垒一片苍茫，烽火也显得冷清；
translation.en: The old fort stood grey and lonely, its beacon fires cold;

translation.zh: 广阔的荒原阴沉沉的，白雪纷飞。
translation.en: over the dark, vast wilderness white snow was flying.

translation.zh: 董大先拨商弦，再弹角弦和羽弦，
translation.en: Dong Da first brushes the shang string, then the jue and yu,

translation.zh: 四周野外的秋叶好像受了惊，沙沙落下。
translation.en: and all around, the autumn leaves fall rustling as if startled.

translation.zh: 董先生啊，
translation.en: Master Dong,

translation.zh: 你的琴声能感动神灵，
translation.en: your music reaches the spirits;

translation.zh: 连深山里的精怪都偷偷跑来听。
translation.en: even the spirits of the deep hills creep out to listen.

translation.zh: 弹得慢了又快，全都得心应手；
translation.en: Slow, then fast, it all flows from your fingers;

translation.zh: 曲调好像要走了，又转回来，像是有感情。
translation.en: the tune seems to leave, then turns back, as if it had feelings.

translation.zh: 像空山里的百鸟，散开了又聚拢；
translation.en: Like a hundred birds in empty hills, it scatters and gathers;

translation.zh: 像万里浮云，一会儿阴一会儿晴。
translation.en: like clouds over ten thousand li, it turns dark, then bright.

translation.zh: 又像失群的小雁在夜里嘶哑悲鸣，
translation.en: It sounds like a lost young goose crying hoarsely at night,

translation.zh: 像胡地的孩子舍不得母亲时撕心裂肺的哭声。
translation.en: like the heartbroken cries of the northern children who would not let their mother go.

translation.zh: 河流因此平静了波浪，
translation.en: The river stills its waves for it,

translation.zh: 鸟儿也停止了鸣叫。
translation.en: and the birds stop singing.

translation.zh: 像远嫁乌孙的公主思念遥远的家乡，
translation.en: It is like the princess married to faraway Wusun, missing home,

translation.zh: 像远嫁逻娑的公主在风沙里生出的哀怨。
translation.en: like the sorrow of the princess in the sandy winds of Luosuo.

translation.zh: 低沉的琴声忽然变调，变得轻快洒脱，
translation.en: Then the low, deep sound suddenly changes and turns light and free,

translation.zh: 像大风吹过树林，雨点落在屋瓦上，
translation.en: like a long wind through the woods, like rain on the roof tiles,

translation.zh: 像喷涌的泉水飒飒地飞上树梢，
translation.en: like a bursting spring splashing up to the treetops,

translation.zh: 像野鹿呦呦叫着跑到堂前。
translation.en: like wild deer calling yōu yōu as they run up to the hall.

translation.zh: 长安城连着东边的门下省，
translation.en: In Chang'an the city joins the East Wing,

translation.zh: 中书省正对着青琐宫门。
translation.en: and Phoenix Pool faces the Blue-Ring Gate.

translation.zh: 那里有位大才子，把名利看得很轻，
translation.en: There a man of great talent cares little for fame or gain;

translation.zh: 天天都盼着你抱着琴去。
translation.en: day and night he hopes you will come with your qin.

background.zh: 董大就是董庭兰，盛唐时有名的琴师，最擅长弹琴曲《胡笳》。他是房琯的门客，房琯很器重他。房琯在天宝年间做过给事中，这首诗大约就写在那时（一说746年前后）。李颀听董大弹琴，写下这首诗，赞美他的琴艺，最后几句又是写给房琯的，称赞房琯不重名利、爱惜人才。
background.en: Dong Da was Dong Tinglan, a famous qin player of the high Tang, best known for the qin piece "Hujia". He was a guest in the household of Fang Guan, who thought very highly of him. Fang Guan served as a secretary (jishizhong) during the Tianbao years, and the poem was probably written then (some say around 746). Li Qi heard Dong Da play and wrote this poem to praise his skill. The last lines are addressed to Fang Guan, praising him for caring little about fame and gain and for valuing talent.

author_note.zh: 李颀（约690—约751），盛唐诗人。他的边塞诗很有名，比如《古从军行》。他也特别会写音乐，《听安万善吹觱篥歌》和这首诗都是用一连串的比喻，把看不见的声音写得像能看见一样。
author_note.en: Li Qi (about 690 to about 751) was a poet of the high Tang. He is famous for frontier poems such as "An Old Army Song". He was also especially good at writing about music. In "Hearing An Wanshan Play the Bili Pipe" and in this poem, he uses chain after chain of comparisons to make sounds you cannot see feel like pictures you can.

appreciation.zh: 音乐是看不见的，李颀却把它画成了一幅幅画。开头先讲曲子的来历：蔡文姬在北方作曲，胡人流泪，汉使伤心，荒原上烽火寒冷，大雪纷飞，一下子把人带进悲凉的气氛。然后董大开始弹琴：秋叶被惊落，山里的精怪跑来偷听。琴声忽快忽慢，像百鸟散了又聚，像浮云阴了又晴，像失群的小雁，像哭着找妈妈的孩子，连河水和鸟儿都安静下来。后来调子一转，又变得轻快：大风吹林，雨打屋瓦，泉水飞溅，野鹿奔跑。读这首诗，就像跟着琴声坐了一趟过山车。最后几句笔锋一转，夸房琯爱惜人才，也是说董大遇到了知音。
appreciation.en: Music cannot be seen, yet Li Qi paints it as picture after picture. He begins with where the tune came from: Cai Wenji making it in the north, the northern people weeping, the Han envoy heartbroken, cold beacon fires and flying snow on the wilderness. At once we feel the sadness. Then Dong Da starts to play. Autumn leaves fall as if startled, and mountain spirits creep up to listen. The music goes fast and slow: like a hundred birds scattering and gathering, like clouds turning dark and bright, like a lost young goose, like children crying for their mother, until even the river and the birds fall silent. Then the tune changes and turns light: wind in the woods, rain on the tiles, a spring splashing up, deer running. Reading it is like riding a roller coaster of sound. In the last lines the poem turns to praise Fang Guan for valuing talent, which also says Dong Da has found someone who truly understands him.
